label: D1 after an a2 choice that rarely led to S1
explanation: Fires only at D1 (never at GO or D2), mainly on the step right after a trial where the agent chose a2 and the rare transition took it to S1 (prev_action==2 & prev_common==0, which is the same as prev_state==1). Dev: precision 0.85, recall 0.64, mass recall 0.77. It fires whether or not that trial was rewarded; the top activations are mostly unrewarded ones in S2-good blocks, where the agent goes on choosing a2. About 17% of the activation mass sits at the first D1 of each window (rel -3). There the previous trial is outside the window, so the predicate cannot see it. The examples suggest those cases fit the same pattern (a2 chosen, value around 7.1-7.5, policy logit favouring a2). Weaker activations (lowest quartile) also show up at D1 after a1-common trials, especially unrewarded ones followed by a switch to a2. Adding the upcoming choice (action==2) raises precision to 0.89 but lowers recall, so it was left out. The predicate uses only observed variables: the previous choice and its reached state are both visible by this D1. The feature never fires at D1 after an a2-common (S2) trial or an a1-rare trial.
